title: Preventive Maintenance 101: When to Schedule, When to React
description: The intervals that matter on a school bus route, and the three symptoms that should never wait for the next service window.

props.text: A bus that misses a route costs more than the repair that would have prevented it. Preventive maintenance is not about doing more work — it is about doing the same work earlier, when it is cheap and the bus is already in the shop.

items.label: Every 3,000 miles
items.desc: Oil and filter, chassis lube, a walk of the air system for leaks.

items.label: Every 6,000 miles
items.desc: Brake adjustment check, air dryer cartridge inspection, battery load test.

items.label: Twice a year
items.desc: FDOE safety inspection, stop arm and crossing gate function, emergency exit operation.

items.label: Before summer
items.desc: Air conditioning service. Florida heat finds a weak compressor in June, not in March.

props.text:
Three things should never wait for the next scheduled window: an air pressure drop that builds slower than it used to, any change in how the brakes feel from the driver's seat, and a charging system warning that clears itself. Each of them is a small repair this week and a tow next week.

If you are seeing any of those, book it — our service advisors keep same-week slots open across Tampa, Sarasota and Davenport for exactly this.
